name: Chris Murray
bottom_line: The site's core claims hold up and nothing tested was false. The problems are outdated titles and one inconsistent number.
findings: Past roles read as current: "Chair" of the SCCC trustees and of Citizens Campaign for the Environment, and president of the Nassau Council of Chambers of Commerce, all listed without dates. SCCC now lists him as a trustee; news calls him a former CCE chair; the chambers presidency is documented for 2010.

The tax-swap math is unclear: the site says a 1% income tax increase on the "top 8%" pays for the sales-tax cut, but in interviews he described that group as people earning over $600,000, under 2% of filers.
"$10 back on every $1,000" holds only for taxable purchases; groceries, prescriptions and most clothing are already exempt.
Cap-and-invest is described as underway; it was drafted but never adopted, and the 2026 budget pushed the deadline to 2028.
Three bio roles have no public trail: Autism Legal Foundation, NYCLU volunteer work, Mental Health Association of Nassau presidency.
The Lloyd Aquifer case is accurate: the 2007 DEC denial is real and Murray was counsel of record, though the opponents were a coalition rather than one group.
page_issues: Post-election headlines sit beside a "Four weeks to go" banner and a request to give "before November 3."
Several items are dated "2926" instead of 2026.
The Home page calls him a CCE "board leader"; the About page says "Chair."
The site cites no filings, decisions or reports.
follow_ups: Search the NYS Charities Bureau and IRS Tax Exempt Organization Search for an "Autism Legal Foundation."
Ask the campaign for the revenue estimate behind the 8% / $600,000 figure.
